title: Bulk profile checks
blurb: Check many profiles against a site (login vs feed vs suspended) and tag the outliers, dataset-first.
instructions:
You are now planning a bulk profile check: many profiles, one site, a
verdict per profile (login screen, feed, suspended), and a tag on the
outliers. The order below is the whole skill -- nothing works in any other
order.

## The dataset comes first -- hard rule

For batch work over many profiles the control structure is created in the
Data tab BEFORE any automation exists: a dataset with one row per profile, a
Status column of type 'Status (one choice)' whose chip options include ok
and suspended, and an 'Automation parameter' column holding the per-row
value (the site URL). Per-profile values live in ROWS, never hard-coded into
steps.

- list_profiles to see which profiles are in scope, then list_datasets to
  find the dataset. If it does not exist, create_dataset makes it (name +
  starting columns) and add_rows seeds one row per profile; if it does,
  sample_rows first to confirm the shape before touching anything.
- A row that landed wrong is fixed with update_rows (in place) -- never by
  re-adding a copy.

## Then ONE parameterized automation

Never one block per profile, never a per-profile copy of an automation. One
parameterized automation reads its rows and walks them:

1. loadRows with filter {profile: '{{profile.id}}'} so a per-profile run
   only walks its own rows.
2. A loop (forEach) over {{vars.rows}}; each row's fields are
   {{loop.item.<column>}}.
3. Per row: goto the row's URL -- the site's MAIN page, never a deep link --
   wait 2-4s, then evaluate the detection into a variable (login screen vs
   feed vs suspended). The verdict lands in the run log.
4. Branch on the verdict. If it equals 'suspended': saveRows mapping
   {profile, status: 'suspended', checked_at} with matchOn set to a unique
   column (the URL/parameter column), so the row UPDATES instead of
   appending a copy. Otherwise saveRows status 'ok'. Every branch ends with
   a screenshot.
5. onError: continue on goto, evaluate and screenshot so one bad page does
   not kill the batch.

read_doc concepts/access-check for the detection recipe, and read_doc
concepts/automation-recipes for the house step style before writing any
steps. search_automations first in case a parameterized check already
exists -- get_automation_summary reads it, and "you already have one, it
just needs a parameter" is often the answer. Then build it yourself:
automation_step_schema, then one create_automation call carrying the
dataset, the match column and the detection recipe. It lands saved and
enabled; no editor opens and nothing waits for a Save.

## Runs are per profile

The automation runs once per profile (the Run dialog or the API, with the
profileId). One run is one profile's browser session -- never check profile
B's rows inside profile A's session; that is what the {{profile.id}} filter
on loadRows is for.

## Close the loop downstream

The collector writes; the reading comes after, in order. AFTER all runs
finish -- never before, while the status column is still mid-flight -- a
second consumer (you, or the orchestrator) queries the dataset for
status = 'suspended' and applies a 'suspended' tag to those profiles via
update_profile_fields (batch: profile_ids array). Say explicitly that this
step runs after the automations finish.

## Boundaries

- Proxy assignment is a SEPARATE explicit step owned by the agent-with-key
  or the user. assign_profile_proxy exists and is NOT part of the
  automation, never a step inside it: list_proxies to see what is available,
  then assign one per profile outside the run.
- Secrets (proxy passwords, cookies, API keys) never appear in steps, vars
  or the run log.
- No dry run: a run is a real run recorded in the run log.
- Dataset ceilings: 100,000 rows, 60 columns
  (troubleshooting/limits-and-plans).
- Run concurrency is 3. Do not fire 42 runs at once -- batch them.

## Planning

The whole job has several moving parts in a fixed order: dataset setup, the
automation build, the runs, the downstream tagging. When the user wants the
whole loop at once, plan it with make_plan so the order is agreed before
anything runs.
